ut_right_fork_2.blurb: The Right Fork is one of the three main zones of Joe's Valley, a high desert bouldering destination in central Utah near Orangeville and Castle Dale. It is entirely bouldering on fine-grained sandstone, with problems from V0 to about V10 and a strong middle band from V2 to V6. Climbing tends to be powerful, with overhangs, compression and slopey top-outs. The canyon holds dozens of boulder areas, including Man Size, The Perimeter, Boy Size and Dairy Canyon. The sun leaves the canyon early in the day, so mornings are the better time to climb. Fall is the prime season, spring is also good, and summer is usually too hot. Sandstone is weak when wet, so let it dry.

ak_seward_highway_2.blurb: The Seward Highway corridor south of Anchorage holds most of the rock climbing near the city. Much of it is on road cuts beside the highway, with more on natural formations off the road. Rock quality is variable: loose and chossy in places, with some good crags among them, so a helmet matters. Sport routes are the largest share, then trad, with boulders, top-ropes and a little ice and mixed. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.13, most around 5.10 and 5.11. Pivot Point is the biggest crag and is usually shady and sheltered from the noise of the road. Sunshine Ridge, Sky Pilot, Dino Head and Bird Creek Boulders are other notable stops.

az_west_stronghold.blurb: West Stronghold is the larger western half of Cochise Stronghold, in the Dragoon Mountains of southeastern Arizona. Pink granite domes, slabs, pinnacles and canyons rise from oak savannah, a rocky wonderland with a remote, backcountry feel. Trad leads, with a good amount of sport and a large bouldering area. Grades mostly run from 5.8 to 5.12, centred on 5.10, with boulder problems in the lower V grades. Many routes are multi-pitch and some approaches are long and rough, so climbs can be committing. The Sheepshead, Council Rocks, Isle of You and Sweet Rock are major areas. Winter is a strong season thanks to year-round sunshine, while summer brings extreme heat.

ca_keller_peak.blurb: Keller Peak is in the San Bernardino Mountains above Running Springs, with crags scattered through dense pine forest across a wide range of elevations. A fire lookout sits on the summit. The area mixes bouldering, trad, sport and top-rope, with boulders and trad the biggest parts. Bouldering is mostly easy to moderate, and roped routes run from about 5.7 to 5.12, with a bulge at 5.10. Hungover Wall, Dinosaur Rocks and Children's Forest are the larger roped zones, and Keller Peak Bouldering is the biggest boulder zone. The rock on at least some crack climbs is very sharp, so tape helps. Bouldering is possible for much of the year.

wy_jackson_hole.blurb: Jackson Hole is the valley beside Grand Teton National Park, where most visitors head for the big peaks but lower crags offer cragging when the weather is poor or you want harder sport. Sport climbing is the largest share, followed by alpine routes and boulders, with little trad. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.13, most at 5.10 to 5.12, and boulders cover easy to hard. Swift Creek Canyon is the biggest sport area. Rock Springs Buttress is a west-facing granite buttress with afternoon sun and routes up to several pitches. Jackson Hole Mountain Resort, Gros Ventre River Canyon and Hoback Shield add moderate options. Mountain weather can be unreliable.

ca_castle_rock_area_bouldering.blurb: This is a bouldering area in the Santa Cruz Mountains south of San Francisco, around Castle Rock State Park and neighbouring Sanborn County Park. The boulders are sandstone, rounded and sculpture-like, with tafoni pockets and smooth tops that often lack holds, so footwork and friction matter more than pulling hard. Nearly everything is a boulder problem, from V0 up to V7 and beyond, with an even spread across the lower and middle grades. The setting is wooded, with trees filtering the light. Castle Rock Loop and the Indian Rock side of Sanborn are the biggest zones, along with Sunnyvale Mountain and Biddles. Sandstone weakens when wet, so give it time to dry after rain.
